textPlacement.assessment: Both contexts preserve the all-age book invitation and the source’s simpler-to-longer language and page-handling progression.
Both contexts support responding to gestures, sounds and words with unhurried shared conversation, without requiring speech.
Both contexts preserve ordinary open-ended home play and identify the separate pretend-play example as around two and a half or later.
Both contexts retain the toddler-wide family language alternatives without converting the multilingual anecdote into a fluency timetable.
Both contexts retain the appendix’s all-age shared music and rhythmic language possibilities with interest guiding participation.
Both contexts preserve the distinct object, matching and vocabulary-card ages, identical-before-similar progression and over-three formal testing limit.
Both contexts retain child-led outdoor noticing and quiet observation without prescribing a fixed skill or age.
Both contexts preserve movement as varied possibilities chosen by current ability, with differing equipment ages and support acknowledged.
Both contexts retain Davies’s attributed toddler screen perspective and distinguish later family anecdotes from promised outcomes.
Both contexts retain current-interest selection, complete materials and adult modeling or shared return without an independent work-cycle requirement.
Both contexts retain genuinely inaccessible small-part storage and shared-space arrangements suitable to children of differing ages.
